scope: Bounded public metadata and official rules research; no order books, registry writes, strategy, or execution
strict_standard: Complementary positions must have equivalent payoff treatment across every material settlement state.

family_rule_provenance.kalshi: Each public series record links a contract-terms PDF. Those terms state that they apply to the contract; representative child rules repeat the relevant exceptional-state windows.
family_rule_provenance.polymarket_us: The official Sports FAQs state default game-level rules unless contract terms specify otherwise. Representative moneyline descriptions provide target-specific postponement language and end times.
family_rule_provenance.precedence_boundary: Observed target-specific language is retained separately from generic venue guidance; conflicts remain material and are not normalized away.

kalshi_family_summary.winner: Official final result; team must score strictly more points.
kalshi_family_summary.tie: Two tied team strikes settle to 0.50 when no tie strike exists.
kalshi_family_summary.postponement: Rescheduled game must begin within 48 hours of the originally scheduled date; otherwise last fair market price.
kalshi_family_summary.suspension: Before 55 minutes and not scheduled to resume within 48 hours generally yields last fair price; after 55 minutes or when the league declares the game final, observed results govern.
kalshi_family_summary.correction: A clearly erroneous first official result may be corrected before contract expiration; later corrections are ignored.
kalshi_family_summary.sources: Governing league first, followed by a Kalshi-defined media/broadcaster hierarchy.
kalshi_family_summary.expiration: Family terms permit latest expiration one week after the time period; sampled child contracts expire approximately 48 hours after scheduled kickoff and can expire early after a winner is declared.
kalshi_family_summary.settlement: No later than the day after expiration unless outcome review applies.
kalshi_family_summary.fair_market: Determined by Kalshi/the Exchange in its sole discretion.

polymarket_us_family_summary.winner: Official final result from the governing body.
polymarket_us_family_summary.overtime: Included for game-level winner contracts unless target terms say otherwise.
polymarket_us_family_summary.tie: Winner-without-tie contracts settle to 0.50 when no winner is declared.
polymarket_us_family_summary.postponement: Generic guidance carries a game to a rescheduled game before contract expiration, typically two weeks; sampled NFL target descriptions instead use rescheduled to a date within two days.
polymarket_us_family_summary.suspension: Official game threshold controls; if no official result and completion does not occur before expiration, last fair market price applies.
polymarket_us_family_summary.correction: Official review delays settlement; a full replay before expiration governs, while a replay after expiration does not alter the original result.
polymarket_us_family_summary.sources: Governing body first, then Polymarket-defined secondary and tertiary source groups.
polymarket_us_family_summary.expiration: All three sampled moneylines end two weeks after scheduled kickoff.
polymarket_us_family_summary.settlement: Exact final settlement interval was not established.
polymarket_us_family_summary.fair_market: Prevailing fair market price at a specified event, typically the official announcement.

Kalshi requires play to begin within 48 hours; Polymarket family guidance uses completion/rescheduling before expiration, typically two weeks, while target text uses a differently worded two-day rescheduling condition.

The venues use different continuation windows and fair-market reference policies; Kalshi target/family rules do not separately establish the same no-contest rule.
Kalshi defines a 55-minute and 48-hour framework; Polymarket defers to the sport's official-game threshold and contract expiration. Exact NFL-state equivalence was not established.

polymarket_us_family_summary.postponement: All sampled moneylines allow delayed, postponed, or suspended games to be rescheduled within two weeks; otherwise last fair market price.
polymarket_us_family_summary.suspension: Official game threshold controls; if unfinished without an official result through expiration, last fair market price applies.
polymarket_us_family_summary.correction: Official review/replay treatment is bounded by expiration.
polymarket_us_family_summary.sources: MLB/governing body first, followed by Polymarket-defined secondary and tertiary sources.
polymarket_us_family_summary.expiration: All three sampled moneylines end two weeks after scheduled start.

target_specific_overrides.kalshi: No sampled game deviated from its series' relevant continuation rule.
target_specific_overrides.polymarket_us_nfl: All three target descriptions use a two-day rescheduled-date condition while the generic Sports FAQ uses expiration, typically two weeks. This consistent template-level conflict is retained as material ambiguity, not treated as equivalence.
target_specific_overrides.polymarket_us_mlb: All three target descriptions conform to the generic two-week expiration policy.

strategic_consequence: Do not continue target-by-target strict-equivalence review of NFL or MLB game-winner/moneyline pairs under the currently observed family rules. Exclude these two family relationships from strict cross-venue arbitrage discovery only through a separate reviewed implementation milestone.
recommended_next_milestone: Add a deterministic, documented discovery exclusion for Kalshi KXNFLGAME/KXMLBGAME versus Polymarket US NFL/MLB moneyline families, preserving diagnostics and the manual VERIFIED-only registry gate; add regression tests and do not generalize to other sports.
